title.en: Work, energy, power and simple machines
Lifting a bucket from the well

text.en: Lifting a bucket from a well, pushing a cart, pedalling a cycle: each needs work and uses energy. Simple machines like levers and pulleys make this work easier.

Work is done when a force moves an object in the direction of the force: W = F x s. The SI unit is the joule.
The work-energy theorem says the net work done on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy.
Energy is the capacity to do work. It exists in forms such as kinetic, potential, heat, light, sound, electrical and chemical energy.
Kinetic energy is 1/2 m v^2 and gravitational potential energy is m g h. Their sum is the mechanical energy.
Energy changes from one form to another but the total remains the same. This is the law of conservation of energy.
Power is the rate of doing work: P = W/t. Its SI unit is the watt, 1 W = 1 J/s.
Simple machines like the lever, pulley and inclined plane let us lift a load with a smaller effort.
Mechanical advantage is the load divided by the effort. A machine that gives MA greater than 1 makes the task easier.
